chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahbub, from Hammad, from Humayd and Jabir al-'Abdi, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: “Indeed, Allah made me an Imam for His creation, so He obligated upon me moderation regarding myself, my food, my drink, and my clothing, like the weak among the people, so that the poor may take my poverty as an example, and the rich may not be driven to transgression by his wealth.”

key_terms.إِمَامًا: a divinely appointed leader for the creation
key_terms.التَّقْدِيرَ: measured restraint and moderation in living
key_terms.الْغَنِيَّ: the wealthy person whose wealth may lead to excess
key_terms.الْفَقِيرُ: the poor person who takes the Imam as a model
key_terms.مَشْرَبِي: my drink and manner of drinking
key_terms.مَطْعَمِي: my food and manner of eating
key_terms.مَلْبَسِي: my clothing and outward mode of living

ai.seo_question: Why did Amir al-Mu'minin Ali عليه السلام live like the poor despite his position as Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام was charged by Allah with living in a restrained and modest manner befitting the weaker members of society. It highlights that Imam-led governance is tied to humility, social empathy, and preventing the moral corruption that can arise from wealth.
